model_type: sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline (SimpleImputer[median] -> StandardScaler -> Lasso), predicts DELTA, trained on real + noise-augmented data (matching src/data/augment_ila.py's exact noise model)
predecessor_model: regression_Lasso_v2_normalized.joblib - GroupKFold MAE 2.774 (real data only, all coefficients zero)
improvement_over_v2: MAE 2.774 -> 2.120 under GroupKFold (24% error reduction), 1.601 -> 0.739 under chronological validation. Unlike v2, this model's coefficients are NOT all zero.
why_augmentation_helps_here: A real, statistically significant regression-to-the-mean pattern exists in the real data alone (recent_shift vs target_delta: Pearson r=-0.368, p<0.000001, n=624 real training rows) - but Lasso cannot confidently assign it a non-zero coefficient from only ~36 rows/instrument (verified: real-only training collapses to all-zero coefficients, same failure mode as v2). Augmentation adds ~1100 additional (X,y) pairs built by perturbing each real row's CURRENT reading with noise ~ N(0, incertitude) - the instrument's own measurement uncertainty - while holding its real historical features and its real future outcome fixed. This reinforces the SAME real pattern rather than inventing a new one, letting the regularized model detect and use it.
honest_disclaimer: This model does NOT beat the trivial persistence baseline (GroupKFold MAE 1.957; chronological MAE 0.522). It is the closest any tested approach has come, and the first with non-zero, mechanistically-verified coefficients rather than a collapsed constant - but it should still not be presented as outperforming simple persistence. See AUDIT_REPORT.md and experiments/audit_v3/FINAL_REPORT.md.
